analysis: Examined the three changed files. (1) ProviderLoop+ModelSwitch.swift:143 adds `selectedModelRecovery.attempt == nil` to modelSwitchMutationsSettled, so a model-switch drain waits for an in-flight recovery load/evict before the coordinator barrier. This tightens the lifecycle fence and does not weaken it. (2) ProviderLoop+Serve.swift: the in-flight recovery task is appended to the shutdown preload-await list (line 565). The model unload loop is replaced by `unloadAllModelsForShutdown()` (line 591); its body is not supplied, so I could not verify that it matches the old semantics (waits for modelsUnloading, loops until modelSlots is empty). That is an unverified contract, not a finding. (3) New ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift adds a capacity-tick-driven background loader for explicitly selected but non-resident models. Evictions are limited to models outside the ordinary selection. Before each eviction it rechecks pause reasons (drain, update, Autopilot, model switch, startup preload, loading/unloading, revision activation), protection, eviction exclusions and the Autopilot victim rules. Loads use allowEviction:false through the normal ensureModelLoaded admission path, so existing weight/self-test/retirement checks are kept (failedSelfTestHashes and isRefusedByRetirement are consulted in the applies check). The daemon-state report exposes only model IDs, timestamps and blocker text, which are already public via heartbeats, so no new sensitive disclosure. No change to the encryption, attestation or App Attest authorization paths, and no new network or IPC surface. Residual: this is a TB-007/T-029 availability and residency behavior (a model reloading after a drain race or an App Attest connection change). Integration questions are whether ensureModelLoaded and unloadModel(forEviction:) enforce serving-drain/authorization state themselves, and whether unloadAllModelsForShutdown preserves the old shutdown guarantees. Neither implementation is in the supplied evidence.
